clue.text: Enormous deficit in nationalised industry

indicators.note: the shortfall sits inside the industry's name, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: coal mining was the classic British nationalised industry, the National Coal Board
a deficit is a loss

explanation.surface: A huge shortfall has opened up in one of the state-run industries.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the coal industry was nationalised in 1947, so 'nationalised industry' is a fair way to say COAL; 'in' puts LOSS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of gigantic size.

clue.text: How a Latvian should regard an Estonian as being blue

definitions.text: How a Latvian should regard an Estonian
definitions.meaning: Latvia and Estonia are both Baltic states, so a Latvian sees an Estonian as a fellow Balt, a CO- (joint) BALT
a deep blue pigment and colour named after a metal

explanation.surface: A question of how one Baltic neighbour views another, ending with the Estonian looking blue.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: split the answer as CO-BALT, a fellow inhabitant of the Baltic states, as Latvians and Estonians both are.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal element gives its name to a strong deep-blue shade; and a co-Balt is a fellow Baltic native.

clue.text: Secure advice to girl who doesn't want to let her hair down

definitions.meaning: to secure a door or building is to fasten it with a key

definitions.text: advice to girl who doesn't want to let her hair down
definitions.meaning: a girl keeping her hair pinned up would be told to put her locks up

explanation.surface: Advice to a girl who prefers to keep her hair pinned up and not relax.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on 'locks' as hair: keep your locks up. 'Let her hair down' also means to relax, which is the surface's misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Fastening a building with a key makes it safe, and a girl putting her tresses up is told to do just that with her locks.

clue.text: Woman graduate who appealed to Solomon

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a woman
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A female graduate once made her case to King Solomon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen of this land visited King Solomon in the Bible, testing him with questions; 'Woman' doubles as surface colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical queen from this kingdom came to Solomon and was charmed by his wisdom.

clue.text: Certainly no description of a doctor with sour disposition

definitions.text: Certainly no description of a doctor with sour disposition

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

indicators.note: disposition means arrangement, so the letters of the word beside it are laid out anew

explanation.surface: A grumpy doctor would never be described as romantically inclined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals an anagram of SOUR, giving ROUS, after A and MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sour-tempered is hardly loving or romantically inclined, which is what the word means.

clue.text: Tom turns over with a twitch, but it's just a ploy

indicators.note: turning over flips the word for the male animal end to end

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a tic is a twitch

explanation.surface: A cat twitching in its sleep turns out to be faking it.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is a male cat, not a name; reversing CAT gives TAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A ploy is a manoeuvre or scheme, a calculated move.

clue.text: Latitude given to dependent student

definitions.meaning: latitude here means leeway or tolerance
money given regularly to a student who depends on parents or a grant

explanation.surface: A student reliant on others is given some freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a margin for error is leeway, and pocket money or a grant paid to a student is the other sense.

clue.text: The herds got agitated and flailed

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the letters of the two words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: The cattle became restless and thrashed about.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain was once beaten with a flail, so flailed and beaten out are the same act.

clue.text: Squeeze a wet pad to ease the pain

definitions.meaning: to squeeze is to press together tightly

definitions.text: a wet pad to ease the pain
definitions.meaning: a damp folded cloth held on an injury

explanation.surface: Instructions for applying a damp cloth to soothe an ache.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing something into less space is one sense; a soaked bandage applied to a wound is the other.

clue.text: Maybe the only thing he was wedded to was his graduate studies

definitions.text: Maybe the only thing he was wedded to was his graduate studies

parts.words: Maybe the only thing he was wedded to was his graduate studies
parts.note: an unmarried man whose only marriage is to his first degree, the arts degree named for single men

explanation.surface: A scholar so devoted to his degree that he never married anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means both an unmarried man and a holder of a first university degree (BA).
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man shares the title of the first university degree, so studies are his only spouse.

clue.text: Warning-it must be cooked like a baba!

definitions.meaning: an old word for a call to arms or alert

definitions.text: it must be cooked like a baba
definitions.meaning: a rum baba is a cake soaked in rum, so it is made 'a la rum', in the French style of cookery naming

explanation.surface: A cook's warning that the dish must be prepared like a rum baba.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A LA RUM, the menu French for 'in the style of rum', as a rum baba is soaked.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic call to arms or alarm; and cooked in the rum style, as a baba is.

clue.text: All those in favour give a positive reply

definitions.text: All those in favour give a positive reply

parts.words: All those in favour give a positive reply
parts.note: in a meeting's vote, everyone in favour is asked to say yes, and their votes are counted together

explanation.surface: A chair calls for supporters at a meeting to say yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural noun means votes in favour, especially in Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: In a vote, the yes votes are counted by that name, as in the House of Commons.

clue.text: Eulogistic archbishop with a Conservative following

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: An archbishop with a Tory following is full of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Laud, a seventeenth-century Archbishop of Canterbury, is a crossword regular; TORY is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Eulogistic means expressing high praise, the same as praiseful.

clue.text: Sir, we resolve to be more intelligent

indicators.note: to resolve can mean to break into parts and recombine, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone tells a knight that they will make up their minds to be cleverer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolve' reads as determine, but here it means break down and reform, an anagram of SIRWE.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word meaning sagacious or clever.

clue.text: Hand over an entry voucher

definitions.meaning: to hand something over to someone
a ticket or permit allowing admission

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an admission ticket to be handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving something to a neighbour is one sense; a ticket allowing admittance is the other.

clue.text: Fine sculpturing material results from a laboratory bloomer

parts.note: an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A lovely carving stone turns out to come from a mistake in a laboratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but it is a flower, the aster.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth white stone favoured for carving vases and statues.

clue.text: Child catches fish, each of which needs 14 lines

parts.note: a son is a child
a fisherman who nets is catching fish

explanation.surface: A boy hauls in fish, each one requiring a lot of line.
explanation.walkthrough: The '14 lines' is the length of a sonnet, not fishing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a poem of fourteen lines, so each of these poems needs that many.

clue.text: Father, turning up, demonstrated that he had no objection!

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up flips the word for dad from bottom to top

parts.note: pa is a word for father
to demonstrate is to prove

explanation.surface: A father showed, by rising, that he was happy with the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses PA to AP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction or endorse something is to raise no objection to it.

clue.text: The French writing about Chinese dynasty with suicidal tendencies

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: about means around, so the writing is wrapped around the dynasty

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: A French writer discusses a Chinese dynasty prone to self-destruction.
explanation.walkthrough: These rodents are popularly (if wrongly) believed to leap off cliffs en masse, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore holds that these Arctic rodents hurl themselves off cliffs in mass self-destruction.

clue.text: Discreditable crib?

definitions.meaning: read as dis-credit-able: able to be paid without credit, paid in advance
a crib is an aid to homework

explanation.surface: A dishonest cheat sheet is disgraceful.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are cryptic: 'discreditable' split as not on credit, and a crib as an aid (AID) for homework, which British schools call prep.
explanation.definitionFit: Settled in advance means without credit; a crib is help for homework, an aid for prep.

clue.text: Mild expletive used to replace an unprintable one

definitions.meaning: a gentle curse like darn

definitions.text: used to replace an unprintable one
definitions.meaning: a printed line stands in for a swear word, as in d--n

explanation.surface: A polite curse is used in place of a rude one.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle curse word, and the printed line that stands in for a rude word's letters.

clue.text: Thin piece of wood. Pine?

definitions.meaning: a fretwork panel or a guitar's fingerboard bar
to pine is to worry or grieve

explanation.surface: A slender strip of timber from a pine tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the wood but is the verb, to grieve or worry.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative thin woodwork is fretwork; to pine is to worry.

clue.text: One is lucky to get it for a song

definitions.text: One is lucky to get it

parts.note: a tune is a song

explanation.surface: Getting something for a song means a lucky bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a song' means very cheaply, the surface's idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck or great wealth is what a lucky person receives.

clue.text: Listen otherwise there is nothing to hear

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Listen hard, yet no sound comes.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of LISTEN is a well-known pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet with no sound, so nothing can be heard.

clue.text: List of things to be done by a general prosecuting officer

definitions.text: List of things to be done

parts.note: DA, District Attorney, is an American prosecuting officer

explanation.surface: A general and a prosecutor draw up a to-do list.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is the US District Attorney, a public prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally Latin for things to be done, it is the programme of a meeting.

clue.text: Dance calling for spirit to some degree

parts.note: rum is a spirit
BA is a degree, Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: A dance that needs some alcohol to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to some degree' looks like 'somewhat' but supplies BA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cuban ballroom dance with a lively rhythm.

clue.text: Heather has to undress before the lad

indicators.note: before puts the undressing word ahead of the plant in the answer

parts.note: strip means undress
ling is a kind of heather

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather must take her clothes off before the boy.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name but is the plant, LING.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth or young man not yet fully grown.

clue.text: Brief item the news chief trimmed down

parts.note: par is short for paragraph, a brief item in a paper
ED, the editor, runs a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor cut down a short piece.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR is journalese for a short news paragraph.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut back or shaved off, reduced.

clue.text: Virginia developing tiny conceit

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters of the small word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Virginia, still growing, has a little self-regard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' turns TINY into NITY after VA.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive pride in oneself or one's looks.

clue.text: Skill needed in small corn-mill to produce a loaf of bread

indicators.note: the skill is placed inside the mill, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a quern is a small hand mill for grinding corn
art is skill

explanation.surface: Skill is required in a little mill to make a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: A QUERN is a hand mill; a QUARTERN loaf weighs about four pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An old measure of loaf, made from a quarter stone of flour.

clue.text: Leave a barren region

definitions.meaning: to leave is to abandon
an arid land like the Sahara

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a wasteland.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning someone is one sense; an arid wasteland is the other.

clue.text: Sell Tate collection, though it means getting one's own back

parts.note: vend means sell

indicators.note: a collection gathers things together anew, so the letters are regrouped in another order

explanation.surface: Selling off the Tate Gallery's collection would be an act of revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collection' looks like the gallery's art but signals an anagram of TATE, ETTA. The Tate is a London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A long feud of revenge, retaliation between families.
